hook: Russell's Title Hopes Die With *5* Laps Left
dek: Verstappen dominated a chaotic Bahrain GP in Malaysia while Russell's title bid collapsed.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Max Verstappen won a chaotic Bahrain GP held in Malaysia after a *90-minute* start delay.

slides.label: The delay
slides.text: Heavy rain caused a wet start, then a software issue made cars crawl during formation laps.

slides.label: The fix
slides.text: FIA issued a software update mid-delay, but the field order got jumbled with no rule to fix it.

slides.label: Race restart
slides.text: FIA restarted the race in original grid order, ignoring usual penalty rules for an unprecedented situation.

slides.label: Russell's collapse
slides.text: George Russell retired from *third place* with five laps left after a power unit failure.

slides.label: Title math
slides.text: Antonelli now leads Russell by *84 points* with six or seven races left this season.

slides.label: Hamilton's comeback
slides.text: Hamilton fell to 17th after a bad tyre call, then fought back to finish *third* for Ferrari.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: Hamilton's comeback from 17th shows why adapting fast when the system fails you matters, on track and off it.

question: Will Antonelli's 84-point lead hold? Yes or no.
first_comment: The FIA's software fix came mid-delay, after cars were stuck crawling behind the safety car.
photo_caption: Verstappen wins as Russell's retirement rocks the title race.
caption_instagram:
Max Verstappen dominated a chaos-filled Bahrain Grand Prix held in Malaysia, while George Russell's title hopes collapsed after he retired from third place with five laps left, according to BBC Sport.

The race started 90 minutes late after heavy rain, then a bizarre software issue left cars crawling on the formation laps. The FIA had no rulebook answer for the mess, and ended up restarting the field in its original order.

Once racing resumed, Verstappen was untouchable. Behind him, Kimi Antonelli now leads Russell by 84 points with only six or seven races left. Lewis Hamilton put on a show too, recovering from 17th to third after a bad tyre gamble at the start.

Will Antonelli's 84-point lead hold? Yes or no.

caption_linkedin:
Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix, held in Malaysia, is a case study in what happens when a system has no plan for the unexpected, per BBC Sport.

A 90 minute delay was triggered by rain, then compounded by a software issue that left cars crawling during formation laps. The FIA's rulebook simply did not cover the scenario, and officials had to make a judgment call on the restart order in real time.

Max Verstappen used the chaos to dominate. George Russell's title bid effectively ended when he retired from third place with five laps left, handing Kimi Antonelli an 84 point championship lead. Lewis Hamilton showed the value of staying in the fight, recovering from 17th to finish third after a bad early tyre call.

The lesson for operators: the rules you write rarely cover the moment that actually breaks you. How you respond in that gap decides the outcome.

Will Antonelli's lead hold? Yes or no.
